skill.name: gene-database
skill.description: Query NCBI Gene and Datasets APIs to search genes, fetch metadata, and run batch gene lookups for annotation workflows.
skill.summary: Search and annotate genes with NCBI Gene, E-utilities, and Datasets API workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: I found no prompt injection, hidden exfiltration, or malicious intent in the reviewed skill files. Most static findings are expected NCBI API usage, placeholder API-key documentation, Markdown examples, and gene identifier handling; the remaining confirmed issue is unrestricted overwrite behavior for a user-supplied batch output path.

remediation.suggestion: Before writing args.output, check whether the file exists and require an explicit overwrite flag or a safe default output path.

remediation.issue: API key handling in command examples
remediation.suggestion: Recommend secure secret handling for NCBI keys, and warn users not to place real keys in shared prompts or logs.
Document that gene queries, Gene IDs, and optional API keys are sent to official NCBI endpoints when scripts run.

content.value_statement: Gene identifiers are hard to validate across species and databases. This skill guides NCBI Gene searches, batch lookups, and concise gene annotations.
actual_capabilities: Search NCBI Gene by symbol, organism, disease, chromosome, pathway, or GO term.
Fetch gene summaries by NCBI Gene ID through E-utilities.
Retrieve structured gene metadata through the NCBI Datasets API.
Batch lookup gene symbols or IDs from a list or comma-separated input.
Save batch results as JSON when an output path is provided.
Reference API endpoints, rate limits, response formats, and common workflows.
limitations: Requires network access to NCBI services.
NCBI API keys are optional but should be handled as secrets.
Gene annotations can change as NCBI updates records.
Scripts do not perform clinical interpretation or variant pathogenicity assessment.

use_cases.title: Validate a gene panel
use_cases.description: Check gene symbols, Gene IDs, descriptions, chromosomes, and organism filters before downstream analysis.

use_cases.title: Build annotation tables
use_cases.description: Convert gene lists into structured annotations for reports, pipelines, or quality control reviews.

use_cases.title: Explore disease and pathway genes
use_cases.description: Search NCBI Gene by disease, pathway, GO term, or publication context to plan research queries.

prompt_templates.title: Search one gene
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup by symbol and organism.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search NCBI Gene for BRCA1 in human. Return the best Gene ID, official symbol, description, organism, and chromosome.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch known IDs
prompt_templates.scenario: Retrieve summaries for exact Gene IDs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch summaries for Gene IDs 672, 7157, and 5594. Compare the symbols, descriptions, organisms, chromosomes, and map locations.

prompt_templates.title: Annotate a list
prompt_templates.scenario: Batch annotation for a small gene set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Annotate TP53, EGFR, KRAS, and BRCA2 for human. Include Gene IDs, descriptions, chromosomes, and any not found results.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a pathway workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced query design across NCBI workflows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an NCBI Gene workflow to find human MAPK pathway genes, retrieve summaries, handle rate limits, and review ambiguous symbols.

output_examples.output: Returns Gene ID 672, official symbol BRCA1, the human organism, chromosome 17, and a short functional description.

output_examples.input: Annotate TP53, EGFR, and KRAS for human.
output_examples.output: Produces a concise annotation table with Gene IDs, official symbols, descriptions, chromosomes, map locations, and lookup status.

output_examples.input: Compare TP53 in human and mouse.
output_examples.output: Lists species-specific Gene IDs, symbols, taxon names, descriptions, and notes that symbols require organism context.

best_practices: Specify organism for every symbol search.
Use Gene IDs when exact records are known.
Keep NCBI API keys out of shared prompts, logs, and transcripts.
anti_patterns: Searching gene symbols without organism filters.
Treating returned annotations as clinical conclusions.
Passing real API keys in shared chat transcripts.

faq.question: Which data sources does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses NCBI Gene through E-utilities and the NCBI Datasets API.

faq.question: Do I need an NCBI API key?
faq.answer: No. A key is optional and only raises rate limits for supported NCBI requests.

faq.question: Can it process many genes at once?
faq.answer: Yes. The batch script accepts comma-separated Gene IDs or a file of gene symbols.

faq.question: Can it interpret clinical variant significance?
faq.answer: No. It retrieves gene metadata and references, but it does not make clinical interpretations.

faq.question: What output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The scripts can print readable summaries or JSON. The references also describe XML and text API formats.

faq.question: Does it work without internet access?
faq.answer: No. The scripts need network access to NCBI services for live lookups.
